steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: I cannot deny your suspicions... It's true that DisCity once had its own army, and went through a long period of territorial expansion. Our history even includes a decade-long period of military dictatorship.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content:
We leveraged our Hypercube advantage to wage wars, invade the Outlands, exploit satellite towns, plunder resources, and even commit countless atrocities...

As the dominant city-state, DisCity crushed every Outland alliance. The reach of its former military conquests far surpassed even what Nirvana achieves today.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content:
It truly was an era defined by fanaticism and extremism, marked by foreign wars and domestic oppression.

It's entirely plausible that during the time, someone secretly sanctioned the development of prohibited weapons, later dispersing them to distant lands through war, with one eventually finding its way into Jasmine's hands.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: All these mistakes were corrected after the DisSea Explosion.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Confronted with BR-000, EDGE scientists worked tirelessly to negotiate a resolution, eventually convincing the old military regime to shift their focus from warfare to catastrophe response. The DisCorps was then restructured into the city-state's anti-Mania framework—marking the birth of the FAC (Framework Against Catastrophe).

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Afterward, we gradually scaled back our expansionist policies, eased tensions among city-states, and dedicated ourselves to reuniting humanity against shared apocalyptic threats.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: In N.F. 106, DisCity first proposed a peace initiative at the Great Expo. Despite facing numerous setbacks, we ultimately secured a comprehensive ceasefire agreement with all city-states by N.F. 107.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: That chapter of our history is now behind us. Today, DisCity is committed to peace. We urge everyone to let go of past grievances and mistrust, so that together, we may heal these wounds and look toward the future...

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content:
...Even with that said, I know you might not entirely agree, Chief.

Jasmine's situation is undoubtedly deserving of sympathy, and your principles are always unwavering. In the few short years since your awakening, you've seen too much darkness to fully endorse many of the city-state's actions.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: In that case, allow me to offer my perspective in defense of my homeland.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The root of all conflict between DisCity and the Outlands has always been Hypercube, and the first and most devastated victim wasn't any distant land... but DisCity itself.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The long-running city-state wars originated with DisCity's anti-colonial movement. The independence war from N.F. 60s to N.F. 80s remains the longest and most devastating conflict ever fought by a single city-state.
You're stunned. Nightingale holds your gaze, and once she's certain you've processed her words, she continues, measured and deliberate.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: In N.F. 24, the leading city-states established DisCity along the shores of the DisSea as a semi-colonial production zone for Hypercubes. Its sole purpose was to extract and export Hypercubes to the colonial powers that funded its operations.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The people of DisCity endured the world's most concentrated Apocalypse of Ashes along the DisSea. Yet, the Hypercubes they mined could not be used for their own protection; instead, it was shipped endlessly to the Outlands, sold at rock-bottom prices.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Industrial goods, capital, food, and water were all strictly regulated. Even after years of painstaking savings, colonial powers could easily strip away the people's wealth with minor adjustments to the prices of essential resources.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...Yes, a stark contrast to what we see today. Back then, DisCity was merely a fledgling mining city, barely surviving on the fringes of a disaster zone. Meanwhile, the colonial powers funding its development had inherited the majority of pre-Nightfall wealth, resources, and heavy weaponry.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content:
DisCity's earliest upper class all originated from prominent powers in the metropoles, remaining loyal to their "homeland" rather than their place of residence.

Those who challenged this system faced brutal suppression. Yet, despite years of oppression, the people of DisCity refused to submit, and resistance began to take shape.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Then, in the N.F. 60s, when DisCity's Nirvana Port sought autonomous trading rights, the metropoles obliterated it with nuclear weapons.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The radiation contamination devastated what was then the most vital independent shipping route, killing at least 150,000 people—a death toll surpassing any subsequent Black Ring outbreak. This catastrophe became the catalyst for all-out war.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: The former military forces mutinied and declared war against the metropolitan coalition. After a prolonged and devastating conflict—one that inflicted heavy casualties and exhausted the city-state's accumulated wealth—they succeeded in expelling the colonizers from DisCity and seizing control of the Hypercubes. They then spent many more years reclaiming their rightful resource cities and satellite towns, ultimately achieving full independence from colonial rule.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: During this brutal struggle, the former military—and eventually the entire DisCity—grew increasingly radicalized. In time... they strayed down a dark path.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: ...I have to admit, trying to justify it like that feels quite pathetic.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, Paradeisos instructed me to explain these things to you, probably in preparation for more important assignments ahead. I believe you'll soon be granted broader authority and intelligence access to manage more complex missions. Naturally, you'll develop your own perspective on these matters. I cannot—and would not—try to sway your judgment.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: But there's one point I think you'll agree on.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: If a city-state holds the only Hypercube mine but lacks the strength and resolve to defend itself, its destruction is inevitable, regardless of alliances, enmities, or even notions of justice. This is simply an objective certainty.
Afterward, you walk alone for a long time—so long that you begin to lose track of the people you've met and the conversations you've had along the way.
[Scene Change]
Late at night, Elvira sits alone in the Recreation Area. On the television screen plays a rebroadcast of an interview with Fraser's advisor, Adelaide.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I'm deeply moved to learn that so many have inquired about Jasmine's well-being. Thanks to the tireless work of DisCity's anti-Mania specialists, we're making steady progress in identifying the root cause of her condition.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Jasmine is a civilian from a distant land who was caught in the throes of prolonged conflict and exposed to a forbidden weapon. Her body and mind have been completely shattered. Regrettably, there is no possibility of recovery at this stage.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: She is a tragic casualty of war, and a poignant reminder that we must not relive the failures of history... Through sustained joint efforts, DisCity and Fraser have dismantled longstanding divides, forging unprecedented collaboration. Moving forward, we are committed to deepening our partnership in economics, technology, and security intelligence.
Noticing your arrival, Elvira jumps in surprise and hurriedly turns off the television.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: I... I couldn't sleep.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...Fraser's acting way too eager. That guy "gifted" you a Sinner, then suddenly brought up the FAC and the past war? He's definitely up to something.

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: But I know so little about Outlanders. Even my father rarely mentioned it in front of me. I...

steps.speaker: Elvira
steps.content: ...I don't really understand how actual Outlanders think.
As she speaks, she lowers her head, her mood visibly darkening. She must be thinking of Jelena again.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I understand.
Beyond offering such a simple response of acknowledgment, you find yourself at a loss for words.
[Scene Change] A softly warm-tinted ring Bureau backdrop as Jasmine's special ward
You step into the ward. Jasmine still lies unconscious. She whimpers softly, as if caught in a nightmare.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Her condition is gradually deteriorating. The treatment through the shackles' connection is unsustainable in the long term since the corruption has built up over many years. MBCC has already arranged for her transfer to Banyan Medical College, where she can receive more stable care and where further research into the next steps can be better supported.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Until then, Chief, please don't force yourself to perform the phase two treatment. It would cause you severe harm.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...I know.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Umm... Uhh... No...! Uhh...
Just a little help shouldn't hurt. You sit down beside her bed.

The shackles emit a faint glow, and the connection between you sends a wave of mild dizziness through your senses. Yet as the moments pass, you watch Jasmine's tense body slowly ease. For now, that is enough.
Time passes by, slow and steady, until night at last recedes and sunlight spills gently into the room. Finally, Jasmine stirs, her eyelids fluttering open.
Her vision is still blurry. She vaguely makes out a hazy figure sitting beside her bed.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: ...Chief... is that you?
She squints slightly and looks again, but when her focus returns, the figure has vanished—no one sits beside her.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: Heh, hahaha... Running won't help. I can still smell you... Are you really that scared to face me?
Her fingers trace the indentation along the edge of the bed—a mark left by someone who had remained at her side for a long time. The faint warmth still lingers, refusing to fade.
Slowly, Jasmine's laughter fades into silence. She pulls her hand back, the lingering warmth slipping away, her eyes fixed on the ceiling with a dazed expression.

steps.speaker: Jasmine
steps.content: You really are a good person...
